result.title: EditHero: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Part-Level 3D Editing and Vibe Modeling
result.summary: 3D editing methods are usually tested on a single edit, yet an asset is built through a long sequence of revisions, each of which must implement the requested change while leaving everything else unchanged. We introduce EditHero, to our knowledge the first benchmark for long-horizon, part-level 3D editing, with natural-language instructions and target images for both geometry and texture. A deterministic assembly engine produces the exact target after every edit, and every sequence is reviewed by hand. We use EditHero to compare 2 opposite approaches to 3D editing. Non-agentic methods operate top down, regenerating the object from a learned 3D representation and inferring what to keep. In contrast, LLM/VLM agents operate bottom up, editing through code that inspects the mesh and rewrites only the parts required by instructions. The non-agentic methods often miss the requested change and disturb regions that should stay fixed. Most LLMs follow instructions more closely, and all of them preserve the unedited parts better, but each of their edits takes minutes. We will release the engine and the edit sequences to support research on reliable iterative 3D editing.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 EditHero，一个面向长序列、部件级 3D 编辑的基准，用确定性装配引擎给出每次编辑后的精确目标，并对比「整体重生成」与「VLM 智能体写代码局部改写」两类方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其长程编辑序列与「只改需要改的部件、保持其余不变」的设定，可能与 LVR 中增量更新内部状态、抑制无关区域扰动和长程一致性评价有概念联系，可供核查是否借鉴其逐次编辑的评估方式。
